analysis: The LightGCN trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.595, exceeding the supplied previous best of 0.5737 by 0.0213. Per-category HR@10 was 0.660 for Movies_and_TV, 0.620 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.395 for Electronics, and 0.705 for CDs_and_Vinyl. This supports collaborative graph neighborhoods as a useful representation overall. Electronics remains the weakest category; these results alone do not establish whether sequential information would improve it. The host reported 52.14 allocated GPU-seconds. No test results were available.
code_summary: Trains one independent LightGCN per category using only training-split user–item edges. Each network has 64-dimensional embeddings, three symmetric degree-normalized propagation layers, uniform averaging of initial and propagated embeddings, and a jointly learned item bias. Adam optimizes eight-negative pairwise softplus ranking with embedding regularization; negatives exclude observed training items. Validation selects one checkpoint per category by HR@10, breaking ties with NDCG@10. The generated predictor routes datasets to their single checkpoint, caches propagated embeddings, and scores known users by user–item dot product plus bias. Unknown users use the mean of their history item embeddings. No ensembles or separately fitted scoring components are used.
